topic: Claude Cowork from zero, for people who don't code: what it is, how it differs from chat, who can use it, how to install it, letting Claude interview you instead of writing long prompts, plugins and connectors, everyday uses, where it falls short and a first 30 minutes
audience: Professionals who don't write code, have used Claude chat (or not at all) and keep hearing about Cowork without knowing what it does or where to start
goal: Install the desktop app, run one real Cowork task in the first 30 minutes, using a short request and letting Claude ask the questions, then add one plugin or connector and know which jobs to keep away from Cowork
notes: Anthropic describes Claude Cowork as bringing Claude Code's agentic capabilities to knowledge work beyond coding. It uses the same agentic architecture as Claude Code but needs no terminal, and takes on complex, multi-step tasks instead of answering prompts one at a time. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Official FAQ distinction: Claude Code is for software engineering; Cowork is for non-coding knowledge work (research, analysis, document creation) using the same agentic approach. [https://claude.com/product/cowork]

The intended workflow: describe an outcome, step away, and come back to finished work such as formatted documents, organized files and synthesized research. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

When a task starts, Claude analyzes the request and makes a plan, breaks work into subtasks, runs code and shell commands in an isolated environment on Anthropic's servers, may run workstreams in parallel, and delivers finished outputs to the session, where you can preview and download them. You keep visibility into what Claude is planning and doing so you can steer when it matters. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]
Cowork can produce Excel spreadsheets with working formulas, PowerPoint presentations and formatted documents. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]
Supported file types include Word, PDF, .txt, .md, .html, .json, .csv, Excel, PowerPoint, common images and most code files. [https://claude.com/product/cowork]

Cowork runs tasks in the cloud: work happens on Anthropic's servers in an isolated environment, and sessions and files are saved to your Claude account, so work continues if you close your laptop. Each session gets an isolated, temporary environment that is removed when the session ends. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13364135-use-claude-cowork-safely]

Check in from anywhere: open the same session on another surface to monitor progress, answer Claude's questions, or redirect the work. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

In the new Claude experience, chat and Cowork are merged into one conversation with no mode to choose; Claude decides which tool to use, and a quick question still gets a quick answer. It is rolling out gradually to Pro, Max and Ultra (Team and Enterprise where 'Chat and Cowork unified' is on). You have it if the message box no longer shows 'Chat' and 'Cowork' options. Once an account has it, it can't switch back. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16761823-claude-cowork-and-chat-are-one-claude]

Cowork is available only on paid plans: Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise. In Claude Desktop, chat is available on every plan including Free. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10065433-install-claude-desktop]

Where Cowork runs: Claude Desktop for macOS, Windows and Linux (beta) on all paid plans; web and Claude Mobile on Pro, Max, Ultra and Team (beta on Team), and on Enterprise when an owner enables it; the Claude in Chrome side panel on all paid plans. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Pro costs $20 a month billed monthly, or $17 a month with the annual discount ($200 billed up front); prices exclude applicable tax. Max is $100 a month and Ultra $200 a month (web prices). [https://claude.com/pricing]

The download page claude.com/download offers Claude Desktop for macOS, Windows, Windows (arm 64) and the Microsoft Store; Linux links to docs. System requirements: macOS 13 (Ventura) or higher, Windows 10 or higher, or Linux Ubuntu 22.04 LTS+ / Debian 12+. Cowork on Linux needs hardware virtualization, about 25 GB free disk and at least 8 GB RAM. [https://claude.com/download] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10065433-install-claude-desktop]

To start a Cowork session: open Claude (web, desktop app or mobile app), select 'Cowork' in the message box, describe the task, then review Claude's approach and let it run. To go back to a regular conversation, select 'Chat'. In the new Claude experience there is no 'Cowork' option: you describe the task in any conversation. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15520349-use-claude-cowork-on-web-desktop-and-mobile]

Local file access, browser use and computer use need the Claude Desktop app open and connected, even though sessions run in the cloud. Sessions keep running when the desktop app is closed or the computer is asleep, but tasks using local files, the browser or the computer need the app open. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

On desktop, Claude can read and write your local files directly, but only in folders you have connected. Anthropic advises creating a dedicated working folder for Claude instead of granting broad access, and keeping backups of important files. Claude must get your explicit permission ('Allow') before permanently deleting any files. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13364135-use-claude-cowork-safely]

Your folders stay on your computer; when a cloud task needs a file, Claude fetches a copy of just that file, and those copies are deleted when you delete the session. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15520349-use-claude-cowork-on-web-desktop-and-mobile]

Three approval modes in the message box: 'Manually approve' (Claude pauses for Allow or Deny on actions), 'Automatically approve' (Claude keeps working and reviews each action for safety, blocking unsafe ones) and 'Skip all approvals' (nothing checks Claude's actions; only when you completely trust every action, connector, file and app involved). Auto is rolling out as the default on Pro, Max, Ultra and Team. For work with real consequences (money, messages sent as you, important files) Anthropic suggests staying close or switching to Manually approve. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16761823-claude-cowork-and-chat-are-one-claude]

Global instructions apply to every Cowork session, for tone, output format or background on your role: Settings > Cowork, 'Edit' next to Global instructions, then 'Save'. In the new Claude experience they are part of 'Instructions for Claude' in Settings > Your Claude. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16761823-claude-cowork-and-chat-are-one-claude]

Scheduled tasks: on the Scheduled tasks page, 'New task' offers 'Create with Claude', where Claude asks you questions and then you click 'Schedule', or 'Set up manually'. Type /schedule in any Cowork task or click 'Scheduled' in the left sidebar. Available on all paid plans. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13854387-schedule-recurring-tasks-in-claude-cowork] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Plugins bundle skills, connectors and sub-agents into one package; a plugin you add is saved to your account, so it also works in chat and Claude Code. Plugins are on all paid plans. Type '/' or click '+' to see plugin skills; in Cowork a plugin command can be run by typing /plugin-name:command. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13837440-use-plugins-in-claude]

To install a plugin (older layout): open Customize in the left sidebar, open the Plugins tab, open Discover, select a plugin and click 'Add'. On Free, Pro, Max and Ultra, 'Customize' now reads 'Plugins' in the sidebar, and one Plugins page replaces the separate Skills, Connectors and Plugins tabs: Your plugins appear above the plugins you can browse, quick filters narrow to skills or connectors, categories cover topic, department, industry or everyday life, and public plugins show Verified or Community. Team gets it from 30 November 2026. To find what you've added: Plugins in the sidebar, then Your plugins > Show all. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13837440-use-plugins-in-claude] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17740565-manage-plugins-skills-and-connectors-from-one-plugins-page]

The January 2026 launch open-sourced 11 Anthropic plugins: Productivity, Enterprise search, Plugin Create/Customize, Sales, Finance, Data, Legal, Marketing, Customer support, Product management and Biology research. [https://claude.com/resources/articles/cowork-plugins]

Adding a plugin does not add or sign you in to its connectors; each bundled connector shows Connected, Not connected or Not added on the plugin's Connectors tab. [https://claude.com/docs/plugins/overview]

Connectors let Claude access your apps and services, retrieve data and take actions, and inherit each person's permissions from the connected service. Add them from the chat '+' menu > Connectors > Manage connectors (or Customize > Connectors), then sign in. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11176164-use-connectors-to-extend-claude-s-capabilities]

Claude picks the most precise tool first: connectors, then the browser, then screen interaction (computer use). Computer use is available for Pro, Max and Ultra in Claude Desktop on macOS and Windows, not on Linux; Claude asks permission before using each app. Anthropic recommends not granting it access to sensitive apps such as banking, healthcare or government. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14128542-let-claude-use-your-computer-in-cowork] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10065433-install-claude-desktop]

Official example use cases: organize files ('Organize my Downloads folder by type and date'), process receipts into a formatted expense report, batch rename files with YYYY-MM-DD patterns, research synthesis, transcript analysis (themes, key points and action items from meeting notes, interviews or lecture recordings), spreadsheets with working formulas and multiple tabs, slide decks from rough notes or transcripts, reports from voice memos and scattered notes, and cleaning datasets. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Official 'Try' examples: 'Go through these five interview notes and pull out the top themes, with a quote for each.' 'Research the top project management tools for small teams and write up a comparison. I'll check back later.' 'Turn this analysis into a 10-slide deck I can present on Monday.' 'Find last quarter's board deck in my Drive and summarize what changed since.' 'Every weekday at 8 AM, summarize new messages in my team's Slack channels.' [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16761823-claude-cowork-and-chat-are-one-claude]

Multi-step tasks (running code, creating files, using connected apps and the browser) use more of your usage than a quick question. Tips: group related work into one task, start a new conversation for unrelated work, tell Claude when you only need a quick answer, and check Settings > Usage. All Claude surfaces draw on the same usage limit. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

Limitations: Cowork sessions can't be shared with others (individual artifacts can be). Claude can hallucinate incorrect information and should not be relied on as a single source of truth. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8525154-claude-is-providing-incorrect-or-misleading-responses-what-s-going-on]

Safety: prompt injection needs Claude to read content outside your trust boundary and be able to take actions; Anthropic says the chance of an attack is still non-zero. Watch for unexpected patterns (files or sites you didn't mention, scope creep) and stop the task if something feels off. Switch to Manually approve for sensitive files, accounts or sites, a new tool or plugin, or mistakes that would be hard to undo. You remain responsible for all actions Claude takes on your behalf. Anthropic strongly advises against using the browser to manage financial accounts or medical data. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13364135-use-claude-cowork-safely] [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16607400-use-the-built-in-browser-in-claude-cowork]

Mojeed's own idea (not a product fact): instead of writing a long prompt, give Claude the outcome in one or two lines and ask it to interview you first, one question at a time, then to show its plan before it starts. This fits how Cowork works: it plans first, shows its approach for review, and lets you answer its questions during a task.
